To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we provide an efficient algorithm that learns the natural parameter of the exponential family distribution with sample and computational complexity of $\mathrm{poly}(1/\epsilon)$, which is the first such guarantee for this class of distribution.

(1) the maximum likelihood estimator of an exponential family distribution can be efficiently estimated using a re-parameterized exponential family distribution, and (2) the re-parameterized distribution can be learned in a computationally efficient manner using a simple iterative procedure.
we provide a computationally efficient method for learning exponential family distributions and provide finite sample guarantees that match the best-known sample complexity bounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
learning the natural parameters (and the distribution itself) of an exponential family distribution from i.i.d samples in a computatationally and statistically efficient fashion.

the following question: Can we design computationally efficient estimators for exponential families that are consistent as well as statistically efficient? Our work answers this question affirmatively.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our estimator is computationally efficient, statistically efficient, and consistent for a broad class of exponential family distributions.
our estimator achieves the optimal sample and computational complexity to estimate a $k$ dimensional parameter in the class of exponential family distributions.
we propose an estimator that has the same statistical guarantees as the MLE, but is much faster to evaluate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a computationally efficient method to learn exponential families with a sample complexity that is optimal (up to logarithmic factors) and a statistical error that matches the minimax rate (up to logarithm factors).

we provide a computationally efficient method for learning the parameters of a $d$ dimensional exponential family from i. i. d. samples, with computational and statistical complexity ${O}({\mathrm{poly}(d)})$.

we propose a computa- tionally efficient estimator for a class of minimal exponential family distributions that achieves the optimal statistical rate of estimation and has the same asymptotic distribution as the MLE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for learning exponential families, one can trade off statistical efficiency for computational efficiency.
, in a wide range of settings, the maximum likelihood estimation can be performed in a computationally efficient manner.
one can design computationally efficient estimators for a large class of exponential family distributions that are consistent and asymptotically normal.
